title: Four hundred years of the Granth
hookLine: Sikhs mark four centuries since the Granth was first installed at the Harmandir
tomorrow: Three hundred years of the Guru Granth

lines: A BOOK CARRIED ON SOMEONE'S HEAD.
FOUR HUNDRED YEARS OF THE GRANTH.
cards: The crowd steps aside for a book. It's wrapped in cloth and carried on someone's head, and behind it walks a man waving a chaur, the whisk of honor, the way you would for a king.
At the end of the walk is a shrine standing in a pool, with a raised seat waiting inside. Tradition remembers this as the day the Granth was first set in place at the Harmandir Sahib in Amritsar.
Centuries later, Sikhs counted back to that day and filled the same walkways. Today: four hundred years of the Granth.

teach.b: Tradition says Guru Arjan, the fifth Guru, gathered the hymns of the Gurus before him, added his own, and included the words of saints from other backgrounds, Hindu and Muslim, whose hymns sang of the One.
Bhai Gurdas wrote the volume down as the Guru dictated. Second, the installation.
The volume was carried into the Harmandir Sahib and opened there, and tradition says Baba Buddha was appointed to read from it. Third, the seat.

The story Sikhs tell is that Guru Arjan had the book placed on a high seat, and sat lower himself. The living Guru sat beneath the book he had compiled: the Word comes first, and even the Guru bows to it.
Fourth, the seal. Near the close of the volume comes a short passage known as the Mundavani, at Ang 1429.
In it, Guru Arjan says that on this platter three things have been placed: truth, contentment, and contemplation. Anyone who eats from it, he says, is saved. A feast, set out for whoever comes.

When Sikhs marked four hundred years, they weren't only honoring an old book. They were remembering the day the platter was first set on the table, and noticing that it's still there, open, every morning.

how: In gurdwaras, the Guru Granth Sahib is carried with honor, placed on a raised seat under a canopy, and opened each morning; Sikhs mark the anniversary of its first installation at the Harmandir Sahib with kirtan and readings.

games.q: you're Guru Arjan, and the book you compiled is now installed in the shrine. where do you sit?
games.why: the story Sikhs tell is that the Guru had the book placed high and sat beneath it: the Word first.

practice: If you have a gutka, or a page of gurbani on your phone, open it to any page without choosing; if not, picture a book lying open on a cloth.

Let your eyes rest on one line, then set three things on an imagined platter in front of you, truth, contentment, contemplation, one breath each, then all three together. If you pray, you can say Waheguru softly between them.

wordCard.voice: Mundavani. The seal near the close of the Granth, where Guru Arjan says truth, contentment and contemplation are set on the platter for whoever comes. Today's word.
